Parent guide
Welcome
This pack is for grown-ups who read with a child aged 4–8 at home. You do not need to be an English teacher, and you do not need perfect English. You need tenminutes, a quiet corner and the three stories in this book.
Each story is a Jurassic English original. You can read it here on paper, or open it in the free online reader at books.jurassicenglish.com, where every page has itspictures, read-to-me audio and a question.
Our goal is simple: your child learns to say
what
they
think,
and
why, in English. "I think … because …" is the most important sentence in this pack.
How
to
read
together
When What
you
do About
Before Look at the cover together. Ask: "What do you see? Whatmight happen?" 1 minute
During Read one page. Point at the picture. Ask the Talk
togetherquestion under it. Wait. 6 minutes
After Ask one of the four thinking questions below. Praise thereason, not just the answer. 2 minutes
Finish Colour one box on the progress chart. Stop while it is stillfun. 1 minute
Three
small
rules
1. Wait
ﬁve
seconds after a question. Silence is thinking time.
2. Any
answer
is
a
start. If your child points, draws or answers in Vietnamese, say it back in simple English: "Yes, Sami is tired."
3. Ask
for
"because". "Why do you think that?" turns an answer into thinking.
The
four
thinking
questions
Every Jurassic English lesson follows the same four steps, the Jurassic Thinking Cycle. Here they are in everyday words. Use one or two after each reading.
Step Ask
your
child Listen
for
Look
closely (Analyze) "What do you see on this page? Show me." A detail from the words or the picture
What
matters? (Evaluate) "Was that a good choice? Yes, no or not sure?" A choice, not a "right" answer
Say
why (Justify) "Why do you think so? Say because." "I think … because …"
What
did
we
learn? (Reﬂect) "When do you feel like that? What would you do?" A link to their own life
There is no wrong opinion. A good answer is any answer with a reason from the story.
The
ten-minute
routine
Read one story for two weeks. Children love to hear the same story again, and each time they notice more.
Day Week
1 Week
2
Monday Read the whole story. Talk together on every page. Your child "reads" the pictures to you.
Tuesday Read again. Do Word
fossils. Read again. Ask the four thinking questions.
Wednesday Pages 1–3 slowly. Act out one page. Think
it
through activity.
Thursday Pages 4–6 slowly. Draw a favourite page. Read in the online reader with read-to-me audio.
Friday Put
the
story
in
order. I
can check, then colour the progress chart.
Six weeks, three stories: Mina and the Midnight Drum, then The Lantern With Two Handles, then Lina and the Orchard Map.
When
it
feels
hard
My
child
won't
answer. Answer ﬁrst yourself: "I think Mina feels sad because her smile stops." Then ask, "What do you think?"
My
child
only
says
one
word. Add to it: "Drum. Yes, the big drum is loud."
My
English
is
not
strong. Use the read-to-me audio in the online reader, and ask the questions in Vietnamese. Thinking matters more than the language.
My
child
is
tired. Stop. One happy page is better than six hard ones.
What
you
will
see
After a few weeks most children start to point at clues on their own, use "because" without being asked, and talk about feelings: theirs and the characters'. Keep theactivity pages; they show how your child's thinking grows.
